examples.ko: 전쟁이 끝난 뒤 그 나라는 공산화의 길을 걸었어요.
examples.en: After the war ended, that country went down the path of communization.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 베트남의 공산화 과정을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, I learned about the process of Vietnam's communization.

examples.ko: 공산화가 되면서 많은 사람이 고향을 떠났어요.
examples.en: As the country became communist, many people left their hometowns.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 공산화 직후의 혼란을 그리고 있어요.
examples.en: This novel depicts the chaos right after communization.
My grandfather came down to the south to escape communization.
Eastern Europe's communization took place in the late 1940s.

explain: 역사 수업이나 뉴스에서 주로 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않아요. '민주화', '산업화'처럼 '-화'가 붙어서 어떤 방향으로 바뀌어 가는 과정을 나타내요. '공산화의 길', '공산화를 피하다'처럼 조사와 함께 써요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in history classes and the news, and is rarely used in everyday talk. Like '민주화' and '산업화', the '-화' ending shows a process of changing in a certain direction. It is used with particles, as in '공산화의 길' or '공산화를 피하다'.

examples.en: That movie is fun because it's a fanciful story.
A plan that is too fanciful is hard to carry out.

examples.ko: 동생은 어릴 때부터 공상적인 이야기를 잘 지어냈어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has been good at making up fanciful stories since childhood.

examples.ko: 공상적인 생각만 하지 말고 지금 할 일을 해요.
examples.en: Don't just have fanciful thoughts; do what you need to do now.
That person's dream is a bit fanciful.

examples.ko: 공상적인 소설을 좋아해서 도서관에서 자주 빌려요.
examples.en: I like fanciful novels, so I often borrow them from the library.

explain: '비현실적'과 비슷하지만 '공상적'은 머릿속에서 그린 환상 같은 느낌이 강해요. 보통 '공상적인 이야기'처럼 '-인'을 붙여 쓰고, '공상적이다'로도 말해요. 이야기나 계획이 현실과 멀 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '비현실적' (unrealistic), but '공상적' has a stronger feel of something dreamed up in the mind. It is usually used as '공상적인 이야기' with '-인', and can also be '공상적이다'. It is often used when a story or plan is far from reality.

examples.en: The prosecution submitted the indictment to the court.
They say the contents of the indictment were made public on the news.
The lawyer read the indictment carefully.
What charges are written in the indictment?
Once the indictment is filed, the trial begins.
The reporters waited to get a copy of the indictment.

explain: 뉴스에서 재판 소식이 나올 때 자주 들리는 말이에요. 검사가 재판을 청구하며 법원에 내는 서류를 가리키고, '공소장을 제출하다', '공소장이 접수되다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: You often hear this word when trial news is reported. It is the document a prosecutor files with the court to bring a case to trial, used as '공소장을 제출하다' or '공소장이 접수되다'.

examples.en: They say everyone comes empty-handed and leaves empty-handed.
My grandfather told me not to be greedy, since we come and go empty-handed.

examples.ko: 돈을 많이 모아도 공수래공수거인데 뭐 하러 싸워요?
examples.en: Even if you save lots of money you leave empty-handed, so why fight?

examples.ko: 공수래공수거라는 말이 요즘 더 마음에 와닿아요.
examples.en: The saying about coming and going empty-handed resonates with me more these days.
After going to my friend's funeral, the saying about coming and going empty-handed came to mind.

examples.ko: 공수래공수거를 알면서도 다들 더 갖고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: Even though they know we come and go empty-handed, everyone wants to have more.

explain: 욕심을 버리라고 말할 때 어른들이 자주 쓰는 사자성어예요. 보통 '공수래공수거라고 하잖아요', '공수래공수거인데'처럼 문장 속에서 인용하듯 써요. 재산이나 욕심의 허무함을 말하는 분위기라서 가벼운 농담보다는 진지한 대화에 어울려요.
explain_en: It is a four-character saying that older people often use when telling someone to let go of greed. It is typically quoted within a sentence, as in '공수래공수거라고 하잖아요' or '공수래공수거인데'. It talks about the emptiness of wealth and desire, so it suits serious conversation more than light jokes.

examples.en: That politician made empty promises again.
Promises that are only words easily become empty promises.

examples.ko: 선거 때 한 약속이 공수표로 끝났어요.
examples.en: The promise made during the election ended up being empty.
It's hard to trust someone who only makes lots of empty promises.

examples.ko: 사장님이 월급을 올려 준다고 했는데 공수표였어요.
examples.en: The boss said he'd raise my pay, but it was an empty promise.

examples.ko: 저는 공수표를 던지는 사람이 되고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to be a person who throws out empty promises.

explain: 원래는 돈이 없는 계좌에서 끊은 수표라는 뜻이지만, 요즘은 거의 '지키지 않을 약속'을 비유할 때 써요. 보통 '공수표를 날리다', '공수표로 끝나다'처럼 말해요. 약속을 한 사람을 비판하는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 그 후보는 선거 때마다 공수표를 날려요.
phrases.en: That candidate makes empty promises every election.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지키지 못할 약속을 쉽게 한다는 비판의 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It carries a critical tone, suggesting someone makes promises too easily that they can't keep.

explain_en: It originally means a check drawn on an account with no money, but today it is used almost entirely as a metaphor for a promise that won't be kept. People usually say '공수표를 날리다' or '공수표로 끝나다'. It carries a tone of criticizing the person who made the promise.

examples.en: The air-raid siren suddenly sounded, so everyone took shelter.
Hearing the air-raid siren in the movie was scary.
We stayed underground until the air-raid warning was lifted.

examples.ko: 이 도시에서는 매달 공습경보 훈련을 해요.
examples.en: In this city, they hold an air-raid drill every month.
The news reported that an air-raid warning had been issued.
Where should I go when I hear an air-raid siren?

explain: '공습경보가 울리다', '공습경보를 발령하다', '공습경보가 해제되다'처럼 짝이 되는 동사가 정해져 있어요. 뉴스나 훈련 안내에서 많이 나오는 말이에요. 같은 경보라도 불이 났을 때는 '화재경보'라고 해요.
explain_en: It pairs with set verbs, such as '공습경보가 울리다', '공습경보를 발령하다' and '공습경보가 해제되다'. It appears often in the news and drill announcements. For a fire, the matching alarm is called '화재경보'.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 합병이 다음 주에 공식화돼요.
examples.en: The merger of the two companies will be made official next week.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 교제가 공식화됐다는 기사가 나왔어요.
examples.en: An article came out saying the two people's relationship has been made official.

examples.ko: 새로운 규칙이 공식화되면 모두 따라야 해요.
examples.en: Once the new rule is made official, everyone has to follow it.

examples.ko: 구두로 한 약속은 문서로 공식화되어야 효력이 있어요.
examples.en: A verbal promise is only valid once it is formalized in a document.
That plan hasn't been made official yet.

examples.ko: 협력 관계가 공식화된 뒤 서로 자주 만나요.
examples.en: Since the partnership was formalized, they meet each other often.

explain: 소문이나 구두 약속이 발표, 서명, 문서를 통해 '공식'이 될 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '공식화됐다'처럼 과거형으로 많이 나와요. 하는 쪽을 말할 때는 '공식화하다'를 써서 '정부가 계획을 공식화했어요'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when a rumor or verbal promise becomes official through an announcement, signature or document. In the news it often appears in the past tense, like '공식화됐다'. When the doer is stated, use '공식화하다', as in '정부가 계획을 공식화했어요'.

examples.ko: 이 기관은 공신력이 높아서 사람들이 믿어요.
examples.en: This organization has high public credibility, so people trust it.

examples.ko: 정부 발표의 공신력이 떨어졌다는 말이 나와요.
examples.en: People are saying the credibility of government announcements has dropped.

examples.ko: 공신력 있는 자료를 찾아서 발표해야 해요.
examples.en: You should find reliable sources and present them.

examples.ko: 언론의 공신력은 한번 잃으면 되찾기 어려워요.
examples.en: Once the media loses its credibility, it is hard to regain.
It takes a long time to earn public credibility.

examples.ko: 그 제품은 공신력 있는 기관의 인증을 받았어요.
examples.en: That product received certification from a trusted institution.

explain: 사람 사이의 '믿음'보다 기관, 언론, 제도, 자료처럼 사회가 믿어 주는 대상에 써요. '공신력이 있다/높다/떨어지다', '공신력 있는 기관'처럼 자주 말해요. 친구를 믿는 이야기에는 '신뢰'나 '믿음'을 써요.
explain_en: Rather than personal trust between people, it is used for things society trusts, such as institutions, the media, systems and sources. Common patterns are '공신력이 있다/높다/떨어지다' and '공신력 있는 기관'. For trusting a friend, use '신뢰' or '믿음'.

examples.en: No matter how much I say, it will just be empty words.
Slogans without a plan end up as empty words.
That resolution ended up as nothing but empty words.
If you only make plans and don't act on them, it's all empty talk.

examples.ko: 제 충고가 공염불처럼 들렸는지 동생은 대답이 없었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling didn't answer, maybe because my advice sounded like empty talk.
Don't say things that are nothing more than empty talk.

explain: 말만 있고 실제 효과나 행동이 없을 때 써요. '공염불에 그치다', '공염불로 끝나다', '공염불에 불과하다'처럼 자주 말해요. '공수표'는 지키지 않는 약속, '공염불'은 아무 힘이 없는 말이라는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when there are only words with no real effect or action. Common patterns are '공염불에 그치다', '공염불로 끝나다' and '공염불에 불과하다'. '공수표' is a promise not kept, while '공염불' is talk that has no power.

examples.en: That person is a craftsperson who makes ceramics.

examples.ko: 공예가의 작업실에 가서 나무 그릇 만드는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I went to the craftsperson's studio and watched them make a wooden bowl.

examples.ko: 저는 어른이 되면 공예가가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: When I grow up, I want to become a craftsperson.
Famous craftspeople gathered and held an exhibition.
My friend ordered a small keychain from a craftsperson.
My uncle, who works as a craftsperson, is always busy.

explain: 도자기, 목공, 금속, 섬유처럼 손으로 쓸모 있고 아름다운 물건을 만드는 사람에게 써요. 그림을 그리는 '화가', 조각을 하는 '조각가'와 분야가 달라요. 직업을 말할 때는 '공예가', 만든 작품은 '공예품'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for a person who makes useful and beautiful objects by hand, such as ceramics, woodwork, metalwork or textiles. It is a different field from '화가' (painter) and '조각가' (sculptor). The person is a '공예가' and the thing they make is a '공예품'.

en: public land; land for common use

examples.ko: 이 공원은 시민 모두가 쓰는 공유지예요.
examples.en: This park is common land that all citizens use.
We made a small vegetable garden on the village commons.
Have you heard of the phrase 'tragedy of the commons'?
You must not use common land carelessly.

examples.ko: 이 숲은 오래전부터 마을 사람들의 공유지였어요.
examples.en: This forest has been the villagers' common land since long ago.

examples.ko: 공유지는 여러 사람이 함께 쓰기 때문에 관리가 중요해요.
examples.en: Because many people use common land together, management is important.

explain: 여러 사람이 함께 쓰는 땅이에요. 개인 땅인 '사유지'와 반대로 쓰고, 나라가 가진 땅은 '국유지'라고 해요. '공유지의 비극'은 경제나 환경 수업에서 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
explain_en: This is land that many people use together. It is the opposite of '사유지' (privately owned land), and land owned by the state is called '국유지'. '공유지의 비극' (tragedy of the commons) is an expression that often comes up in economics and environment classes.

examples.ko: 이 사업은 공익성이 높아서 정부가 지원해요.
examples.en: This project has a high public benefit, so the government supports it.
You should think about the public interest before advertising.

examples.ko: 공익성 있는 캠페인에 많은 사람이 참여했어요.
examples.en: Many people took part in the campaign that served the public interest.

examples.ko: 공익성은 낮은데 비용만 많이 드는 사업이에요.
examples.en: It is a project with low public benefit that only costs a lot.

examples.ko: 법원은 그 건물 철거의 공익성을 인정했어요.
examples.en: The court recognized the public interest in tearing down that building.

examples.ko: 방송은 공익성과 재미를 함께 챙겨야 해요.
examples.en: Broadcasting must take care of both public interest and entertainment.

explain: 어떤 일이 사회 전체에 도움이 되는 정도를 말할 때 써요. '공익성이 높다/낮다', '공익성을 인정하다'처럼 말하고, 방송·사업·법 이야기에서 많이 나와요. '공익'은 사회 전체의 이익이고, '-성'이 붙으면 그런 성질이 있는지를 말해요.
explain_en: It is used to talk about how much something benefits society as a whole. People say '공익성이 높다/낮다' or '공익성을 인정하다', and it comes up often in talk about broadcasting, businesses and law. '공익' is the benefit of society as a whole, and adding '-성' talks about whether something has that quality.

examples.ko: 공중제비를 멋지게 돈 선수가 금메달을 땄어요.
examples.en: The athlete who did a great somersault won the gold medal.

examples.ko: 공중제비는 처음 배울 때 조금 무서워요.
examples.en: Somersaults in the air are a little scary when you first learn them.

examples.ko: 공중제비 한 번에 관중이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The audience clapped after one single somersault.
I tried doing a somersault at the swimming pool.
My older brother can even do a somersault.
I fell while doing a somersault and hurt my wrist.

explain: 몸을 공중에서 거꾸로 한 바퀴 돌리는 동작이에요. 보통 '공중제비를 돌다'처럼 '돌다'와 함께 써요. 바닥에서 구르는 '앞구르기'와는 달리 몸이 공중에 떠서 도는 동작이에요.
explain_en: This is the move of flipping your body upside down once in the air. It is usually used with '돌다', as in '공중제비를 돌다'. Unlike '앞구르기' (a forward roll on the ground), the body is in the air while turning.

examples.en: This drama is broadcast on terrestrial TV.

examples.ko: 요즘은 공중파보다 유튜브를 더 많이 봐요.
examples.en: These days I watch YouTube more than terrestrial TV.

examples.ko: 공중파 뉴스는 저녁 여덟 시에 시작해요.
examples.en: The terrestrial TV news starts at eight in the evening.
I was very nervous appearing on terrestrial TV for the first time.
The terrestrial broadcasters broadcast the World Cup together.

examples.ko: 케이블이 없어도 공중파는 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even without cable, you can watch terrestrial TV.

explain: 안테나로 전파를 받아 보는 지상파 방송을 일상 대화에서 이렇게도 불러요. 케이블 채널, 종합편성채널, 유튜브와 구분할 때 자주 써요. 공식적인 말은 '지상파'예요.
explain_en: In everyday talk, people also use this word for over-the-air broadcasting. It is often used to separate it from cable channels, general programming channels and YouTube. The formal term is '지상파'.

examples.en: In front of my mother, my father becomes henpecked.
My friends tease me by calling me henpecked.
I watched a comedy with a henpecked husband in it.

examples.ko: 그는 겉으로는 센 척해도 사실 공처가예요.
examples.en: He acts tough on the outside, but he is actually henpecked.

examples.ko: 공처가 소리를 들어도 우리 집은 평화로워요.
examples.en: Even if I'm called henpecked, our home is peaceful.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 소문난 공처가라서 늘 일찍 집에 가요.
examples.en: My uncle is a well-known henpecked husband, so he always goes home early.

explain: 아내를 몹시 무서워하거나 아내 말을 잘 따르는 남편을 조금 놀리듯 부르는 말이에요. 반대로 아내를 많이 사랑하는 남편은 '애처가'라고 해요. 본인에게 쓰면 농담이 되지만 남에게 직접 쓰면 실례일 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a teasing word for a husband who is very afraid of his wife or does what she says. A husband who loves his wife a lot is called '애처가', the contrasting word. Using it about yourself can be a joke, but saying it directly to someone else can be rude.

en: boasting about a favor; taking credit

examples.en: Don't boast about having helped me.
He takes a lot of credit even for small things.
I didn't help you in order to take credit for it.

examples.ko: 아버지는 자식을 키운 공치사를 한 번도 안 하셨어요.
examples.en: My father never once bragged about raising his children.

examples.ko: 공치사 같지만 이번 일은 제가 다 했어요.
examples.en: It may sound like boasting, but I did all of it this time.
Stop taking credit and let's just eat.

explain: 자기가 한 일이나 남에게 베푼 일을 일부러 말하며 생색내는 것이에요. '공치사를 하다/늘어놓다'로 쓰고, '공치사하다'로도 말해요. 단순한 칭찬이 아니라 듣는 사람이 조금 불편해질 수 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: It means deliberately mentioning what you did or gave to others so you can take credit for it. It is used as '공치사를 하다/늘어놓다' or as the verb '공치사하다'. It is not simple praise, and it can make the listener a little uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 이 선수는 과감성이 부족해서 슛을 잘 안 해요.
examples.en: This player lacks boldness, so he rarely takes shots.
Boldness is good, but you also need to make a plan.

examples.ko: 그 디자이너는 과감성 있는 색 선택으로 유명해요.
examples.en: That designer is famous for bold color choices.

examples.ko: 사장님의 과감성 덕분에 회사가 크게 성장했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the boss's boldness, the company grew a lot.
Investing requires both boldness and caution.

examples.ko: 저는 좀 더 과감성을 기르고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to build up a bit more boldness.

explain: 망설이지 않고 결단력 있게 행동하는 성질이에요. '과감성이 있다/부족하다', '과감성을 기르다'처럼 써요. 좋은 뜻으로 많이 쓰고, 지나치면 '무모함'이 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is the quality of acting decisively without hesitation. It is used as '과감성이 있다/부족하다' or '과감성을 기르다'. It is mostly positive, but too much of it can turn into '무모함' (recklessness).

examples.en: It's already in the past, so let's forget it as bygones.
That matter is all in the past now.
If you cling to the past, it's hard to move forward.

examples.ko: 둘이 싸운 건 과거지사니까 이제 화해해요.
examples.en: The fight between you two is in the past, so make up now.
Don't keep bringing up the past.
Even hard times become things of the past once they're over.

explain: 이미 지나간 일이라 더 따지지 않겠다는 마음을 담아서 '과거지사로 하다/치다', '다 과거지사예요'처럼 말해요. 그냥 '과거'는 시간을 말하고, '과거지사'는 지난 일을 이제는 문제 삼지 않는 분위기가 있어요. 화해하거나 위로할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of not dwelling on something already over, as in '과거지사로 하다/치다' or '다 과거지사예요'. Plain '과거' just refers to time, while '과거지사' has a tone of no longer making an issue of what has passed. It is often used when making up with someone or comforting them.
